note: Contrarian Shark pass, competitor PM angle: the draft is exhaustive but carries an internal Phase-0 contradiction, one gate that cannot pass as specified, one criterion-narrowing escape hatch, and a daily-use gap that a competing plan would close on day one.

findings.message: Every phase carries TWO numbers ('Phase 1 — Phase 0', 'Phase 5 — Phase 4 — Event-Log Spine') and body text cross-references use the inner scheme ('the Phase-3 event envelope' means the header-Phase-5 journal; 'Phase-4 sequencing' means the header-Phase-6 supervisor). Two live numbering schemes in a document that Stage 2 and Foreman will consume mechanically is a misrouting defect, not cosmetics: a wave sequenced against the wrong 'Phase 3' violates the dependency DAG the plan itself declares (journal after data-dir move, supervisor after spike verdict). Collapse to one numbering scheme before Stage 2 or this WILL produce a sequencing error.

findings.topic: Phase 0 self-contradiction — contract shim is a product change that references a not-yet-existing artifact
findings.section: Phase 0 near-term specifics (contract-versioning shim) vs its own deferrals
findings.message: Phase 0's deferral list says 'Any product-behavior change — Phase 0 is instrumentation, spikes, and process artifacts only', yet the same phase ships the frontend↔backend contract shim LIVE ('in the LAST pre-migration release'): new client header on every _postJson, new server 409 path, new banner UI. That is a deployed product-behavior change by any definition. Worse, the shim is specified as 'ANCHOR_BOOT carries a build id' — but window.ANCHOR_BOOT is created by the extraction phase that runs AFTER Phase 0; pre-extraction there is no bootstrap JSON for the build id to ride in, so the shim as written depends on an artifact from its own future. Either the shim gets its own pre-extraction injection mechanism (spelled out), or it moves into extraction increment 1 — as drafted the plan's very first deliverable is unimplementable as specified and contradicts its own phase contract.

findings.topic: byte-parity gate infeasible for the interpolated generate_html blob
findings.message: The gate claims OLD-f-string vs NEW-static output is diffed 'byte-for-byte after {{/}} de-escaping', with Playwright reserved for the bootstrap seam. But increment 3 — the generate_html f-string JS/CSS — contains DATA interpolations by construction (the entire reason the Phase-0 census exists). Post-extraction, every data interpolation becomes an ANCHOR_BOOT read or API call, so the static file is NOT byte-equal to the rendered old output precisely in the regions where the risk lives. Byte-parity is only honest for interpolation-free spans. As written, the plan's central C1 gate cannot go green for the one increment it calls 'the only genuinely fiddly one', which means it will be quietly weakened mid-wave — the exact failure mode Phase 0 exists to prevent. Specify the real comparison now: render BOTH paths against one pinned state and compare post-substitution output, or byte-compare only census-classified static spans with the interpolated spans enumerated and Playwright-covered individually.

findings.topic: legacy-arm residual escape hatch narrows C2 without the amendment path
findings.message: C2 says ALL ~125 dispatch arms 'dispatch through a single declarative table'. Phase 2's gate is explicitly weakened to 'every route has a row + data plane enforced, not zero legacy arms', and closure then offers 'driven to zero OR its residual explicitly carried as named debt'. 'Named debt' is a narrowing channel that bypasses the North Star's amendment rule — the scorecard clause says any narrowing goes through the documented amendment path, yet this sentence pre-authorizes shipping C2 unmet as mere debt. A competitor plan would be pinned to the criterion: either the zero-arm milestone is a binding exit condition of the effort (state which phase owns it), or the residual case is routed through a John-approved amendment, never a debt register.

findings.topic: every deploy kills live PTYs until the final phase — drain ships too late
findings.section: Phase 0 smoke ritual + Phase 5 drain fallback
findings.message: The per-wave smoke ritual restarts the anchor service at EVERY merged increment across all seven phases, and until the supervisor phase lands, restarts kill in-flight jobs and live PTY sessions — John's actual daily use. The plan pre-DESIGNS the graceful drain (park + capture_session_docs + warm-resume seed) in Phase 0 but only SHIPS it in Phase 5/6 'in the same wave as any narrowing'. That leaves the entire extraction, route, hygiene, and journal campaign — the bulk of the effort's deploys — destroying live context on every merge, which strains 'John's daily use never breaks' for months while the fix sits designed-but-unshipped. Ship the drain script as a Phase-0 deliverable (it composes existing, already-tested primitives: close_session, capture_session_docs, W3 resume) and make it part of the smoke ritual from wave one.

C3's bar is 'reports zero divergence'. The gate as designed tolerates a bounded tail window and classifies journal-ahead as OK/crash-residue. Engineering-wise this is defensible, but it is not the locked criterion — it is a redefinition embedded inside a gate implementation. State the delta explicitly (zero divergence AFTER quiescence and journal-ahead reconciliation, with journal-ahead bounded and replayed) and, if that is a narrowing, route it through the amendment path rather than shipping a gate that reports green against a softer bar than the one John locked.

findings.topic: golden corpus of real markdown collides with the no-PII constraint
findings.message: The de-fork gate is 'today's REAL markdown files parsed identically pre/post'. If those files (domains/commercial.md carries proprietary fundraising and relationship detail) are snapshotted into a committed test corpus, the repo's own no-PII/secrets discipline (distro.py scan) is violated and sensitive data gets frozen into git history. Specify now: the golden run executes against the live files in place (uncommitted, environment-local) or against a synthetic corpus that covers every parse construct; a committed real-data corpus is not an option.

findings.topic: one-day auth warn soak under-samples a cron-driven consumer set
findings.message: 'Warn for a soak day' assumes consumers fire daily. This system's callers are cadence-driven: the 5AM healthcheck fires once a day, scheduled tasks and launchers fire irregularly, and the iPad PWA may not be opened for days. A 24-hour warn window can therefore certify a route batch clean while a weekly or occasional consumer is about to be locked out. Bind the soak to coverage, not time: at least one full healthcheck cycle PLUS an affirmative check that every consumer the Phase-0 enumeration listed for those routes appeared in the warn log (or was manually exercised) before enforce.

'Loopback token-authed IPC' is asserted but never specified: same ANCHOR_TOKEN or a distinct supervisor token; whether the supervisor's HTTP surface gets the same default-deny declarative route treatment the effort just built for the dashboard (a second hand-rolled if-elif server would recreate the C2 disease in a new process); and how the token stays in sync across two NSSM services' AppEnvironmentExtra when rotated. install_supervisor.ps1 'clones' the env once — rotation drift between the two services is an unhandled failure row that belongs in the IPC contract table.

findings.topic: 20×-nightly soak has no infrastructure and serializes closure
findings.message: Each of the four new walks must run '20× nightly' before joining the 5AM run, but no nightly-repetition mechanism exists or is planned — that is a new scheduled task (an ops-surface addition the non-goals say this effort doesn't make beyond the supervisor service) and, read literally, ~20 nights of serialized calendar time per walk at the very end of the effort. Define the mechanism now and allow accelerated repetition (20 consecutive runs in one night satisfies the same flake-detection intent) so closure isn't a multi-week idle soak.

'Old dir preserved read-only for a week' is a backup, not a rollback plan. Any rollback invoked after real use resumes on the new dir silently discards the sessions, efforts, and (later) journals written there in the interim. Specify the actual rollback procedure — reverse-migrate new-dir deltas back, or an explicit accept-loss statement with the window bounded — so the 'rollback-able unit' claim is honest rather than nominal.

findings.topic: pre-authorized C1 amendment treats John's approval as mechanical
findings.message: The census step says if markup-emitting interpolations exceed a threshold, 'amend the North-Star C1 bar ... NOW'. Amendments require John's decision; the plan phrases this as an automatic consequence of a script's output. Rephrase as a decision gate: census output → present the evidence and the amendment option to John → proceed on his answer. Also state the threshold numerically before the census runs, or the 'small threshold' becomes negotiable after the fact.

A competing plan would carry rough per-phase wave counts and calendar expectations so the seven-phase sequence (with two spikes, a merge freeze, and a 20-night soak) can be sanity-checked against John's tolerance for a months-long substrate effort. No North-Star criterion demands estimates, so this is demoted — but Stage 2 should surface it.
